artifacts.summary: 4-phase plan (1.75h) replacing the two jq-object-into-head-1 pipelines in literature-briefing.sh with jq -c first(...), plus baseline capture, head -1 audit, and end-to-end verification against the observed failing Logos/Theory sub-index.

memory_candidates.content: Shell scripts running under `set -euo pipefail` must never pipe a jq query that can emit a JSON object or array into a line-truncating tool (`head -N`, `sed -n 1p`). jq pretty-prints objects across many lines by default (`-r` does NOT change this -- it only affects string scalars); `head` reads the first line and closes the pipe; jq receives SIGPIPE and dies 141; `pipefail` promotes the pipeline status and `set -e` kills the script. The failure looks intermittent because it is a 64KB-pipe-buffer race: small objects fit the buffer and jq completes before the reader exits, so many iterations succeed before one large entry crashes the script. Fix by bounding the result inside jq -- `jq -c 'first(.entries[] | select(...))'` or `limit(1; ...)` -- which removes the pipe entirely and also stops the scan at the first match instead of streaming discarded matches. `first(...)` over an empty stream emits nothing and exits 0 under `set -e`, so no `|| true` guard is needed. Adding `-c` alone also removes the race but leaves the fragile idiom in place. Never 'fix' this by removing pipefail or set -e.
